examples.title: Chemical and pharmaceutical data science
facts: About 10 short lectures and 15 two-hour exercise sessions, in Python with Jupyter notebooks
Group project handed in as an executable notebook, pass/fail
examples.summary: Students learn how chemical and pharmaceutical data are represented and analysed: molecular descriptors, machine learning for property prediction, model evaluation and reproducible notebooks. The course ends with a group project on a real dataset.

short.anchor: Molecular property prediction, used to rank compounds before a candidate is chosen
short.deliver: Each two-hour exercise session is planned as a 4Cs sequence. Its practice block feeds the group project.

anchor.why: The course's machine-learning work predicts molecular properties. In industry that ranking happens during lead optimisation, and early screening of hits in lead identification uses the same molecular representations.

targets.why: We assume students arrive able to fit a simple model but used to reporting a single accuracy number. The project should show how the conclusion changes with the data split and resampling.
We assume students have run notebooks written by others. The exam asks for an executable notebook, so another group should be able to re-run it from the raw data.

design.format: One two-hour exercise session (120 minutes), one of about 15

blocks.title: Would you trust this prediction?
blocks.activity: In pairs, students look at one predicted solubility value and say what they would need to see before using it to drop a compound.

blocks.title: One accuracy number hides a lot
blocks.activity: Short input with three plots of the same model: a random split, a scaffold split and a calibration curve.

blocks.title: Stress-test your project model
blocks.activity: Each group re-runs its own model with a scaffold split and a bootstrap, writes down how the conclusion changes, and saves the notebook so another group can re-run it.

blocks.title: One sentence for the report
blocks.activity: Each group writes the claim its evaluation supports and one limitation, then reads both out.

examples.title: Workshop for the teachers of Methods and Procedures in Clinical Drug Development
facts: People Development, tailored workshop (imagined for this example)
A hypothetical teaching team for the course
MSc Pharmaceutical Sciences, 7.5 ECTS; students write a clinical-trial protocol
examples.summary: In this real course, students write a clinical-trial protocol from a medical case. This imagined People Development workshop helps the course's teachers mark the statistics in those protocols and judge how students use AI tools.

short.anchor: Trial-protocol teaching, where designs are powered, analysed and reported
short.deliver: Two half-day workshops. Teachers practise on the medical case they set their own students.

anchor.why: A protocol is designed for Phase I, II or III trials, and its analysis choices must hold up when a regulator reviews them.

targets.why: We assume the teaching team can run a standard test. Judging a student's analysis plan also means choosing and interpreting tests for the trial in question, including multiplicity.

targets.competency: What can AI be used for? What can it not be used for?
targets.why: We assume the team has no shared way yet to decide which uses of AI in protocol writing are fine, which are poor and which are unsafe.

blocks.title: The section you dread marking
blocks.activity: Teachers stand at a wall and sort anonymised statistics sections from past reports into 'confident to mark' and 'unsure'.

blocks.title: Three things every analysis plan must settle
blocks.activity: Short input on the estimand, multiplicity and sample size, with one annotated protocol page on screen.

blocks.title: Rework your own case
blocks.activity: In pairs, teachers write the analysis section a strong student should produce for the case they set, then swap and review it against a checklist.

blocks.title: AI: good fit, poor fit, unsafe
blocks.activity: Teachers place eight example uses of AI by students on a three-zone floor map and argue over the borderline cases.

blocks.title: One change before the next course run
blocks.activity: Each teacher writes one change to the protocol assignment, with a date, and reads it to the group.
